Definition: from G3084; a ransoming (figuratively):--+ redeemed, redemption.
BiblicalUsage: The word names redemption, the ransoming itself, and it appears where Scripture celebrates the rescue God has already worked. Zechariah blesses the Lord God of Israel because He has visited and redeemed His people, and Anna spoke of the child to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem. Hebrews says Christ entered the holy place by His own blood, having obtained eternal redemption for us.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe redemption is eternal because the blood that bought it is Christ's own, and no one can undo what He has finished. I hold that Anna and Zechariah were right to rejoice, because the redemption they had waited for was standing in front of them.
